evidence:
io.lisp:6978-6983
  "The segment's size ... Not a positive number of units is a fault: init and every extension leave whole units."
  (let ((st (fnn-check-regular path)))
    (unless st (fnn-refuse "no log segment at ~a" path))
    (sb-posix:stat-size st)))
io.lisp:6406-6409 (fnn-log-open-segment)
  (unless (fnn-core 'fn-lg-extent-okp extent unit)
    (error 'fnn-usage-error
           :message (format nil "log extent ~a is not a positive number of ~a-octet units" ...)))
fnn-usage-error is a subtype of fnn-store-error (io.lisp:98), and fnn-main maps it to the usage exit (8615-8617).
fix: Have fnn-log-observed-extent perform the check its docstring promises and signal a named store-open refusal or fault (log-damaged). Keep fnn-usage-error only for the developer `log` verb's typed EXTENT argument.
reviewer: Confirmed as written. fnn-log-observed-extent (io.lisp:6978-6983) does not perform the whole-units check its docstring promises. fnn-log-open-segment (6406-6409) signals fnn-usage-error, which fnn-main maps to the usage exit before the generic store-error clause (8615-8617). Inside the open, fnn-recover-log's fnn-store-error handler turns the same condition into the fault "cannot reconstruct committed history" (7704-7706). The usage-exit path is reachable mainly through `log scan-store`, which has no prior open. The export and checkpoint history readers read only segments the open already scanned under the same extent check, so they would show the usage exit only if the damage happened after the open. In practice the problem is a misclassified exit code on a diagnostic verb, plus the docstring mismatch.
scenario: A closed segment is truncated by disk damage or an operator copy. History readers (fnn-log-read-closed-segment from export or checkpoint, 7530-7532) and `log scan-store` (8135-8136) exit with the usage code (5) and "fn-host: error: log extent ... is not a positive number". Store damage is reported as a typing mistake by the caller. During the open, the same condition becomes "cannot reconstruct committed history" (fault), so one damage has two different outcome classes depending on the verb.
title: A damaged segment size is reported as a usage error; fnn-log-observed-extent's docstring claims a check the code lacks
